name: Can a sunroom be built on top of an existing concrete patio?

mainEntity.name: Can a sunroom be built on top of an existing concrete patio?

acceptedAnswer.text: A sunroom addition requires structural foundation support, such as concrete footings, piers, or a poured stem-wall foundation built below the local frost line. In northern Utah climates like Salt Lake City, Sandy, and Draper, standard four-inch patio slabs are rarely thick enough or engineered to carry the structural dead load of framed walls, heavy glass, and snow loads on the roof. A contractor must inspect your patio to determine if it can be structurally underpinned or if it must be excavated and replaced with a code-compliant foundation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Only if the patio slab meets local footing and frost-depth engineering requirements. Most standard patios must be reinforced or replaced with proper structural footings.
